title: The Provision of the Upper Fly River
premise: When a flood on the Upper Fly River exposes a bronze chest bearing the seal of a vanished colonial administration, Xanthe Fairweather—hiding in the bush from his famous father's shadow—finds himself hunted by a mining consortium, a descendant of the chest's drowned custodian, and his father's expedition, all claiming the treasure. Following the river to its forbidden headwaters, Xanthe learns the chest holds not gold but records of atrocities the consortium's founders committed and buried. In the climax, as the monsoon breaks, Xanthe must choose between destroying the evidence to protect the river people who sheltered him or revealing it and surrendering his anonymity. He chooses truth, giving the chest to the custodian's descendant and the story to the world, finally claiming his own name.
about_author: B. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping waterways no government would officially acknowledge. Underhill now writes from a houseboat that changes ports more often than most people change addresses.

chapters.title: What the River Surrenders
chapters.summary: Xanthe, living off-grid as a hired digger under a false name, is hired to survey flood damage and unearths the seal-stamped chest. He pockets a bronze medallion before the site is seized by consortium men. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into dread as he realizes the chest was hidden, not lost—and that someone was waiting for it to surface.

chapters.title: The Custodian's Daughter
chapters.summary: Amara, granddaughter of the chest's last guardian, tracks Xanthe down, not for treasure but for the medallion, the key to a ledger hidden upstream. Consortium enforcers burn Xanthe's camp, forcing the two into uneasy alliance. POV: alternating Xanthe and Amara. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion giving way to grudging respect as their secrets—his identity, her family's guilt—begin to surface.

chapters.title: Upstream of Every Law
chapters.summary: Racing the monsoon, Xanthe and Amara ascend the forbidden gorge with the consortium's mercenaries closing behind and Xanthe's father's expedition blocking the river ahead. At the headwaters cave, they find the ledger documenting the consortium founders' massacre of the custodian's village. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: grief and fury—her inheritance is not gold but a debt of witness—while Xanthe confronts his father and refuses to be reclaimed.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Trapped in the cave as the monsoon hits, Xanthe and Amara outwit the mercenaries, flooding the gorge to cover their escape. Xanthe chooses to broadcast the ledger rather than bury it, surrendering his anonymity to shield Amara from prosecution. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: resolution—justice delivered outside the courts, his father's shadow finally broken, and a new identity built on truth rather than disappearance.
